title: Microsoft Viva: targeted audience surveys in the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, default state, audience restrictions and control instructions are supported by Microsoft's records and documentation. Minor corrections should acknowledge inconsistent licensing documentation and identify the role-assignment and exclusion-list checks that have no controls-table rows.

claims.fix: After this sentence, add: 'Microsoft documentation is inconsistent: the general Viva Pulse licensing requirements page lists Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint and the admin-led trial for the full premium experience, but does not list Microsoft Copilot.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/get-started/licensing-requirements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Integrating Pulse results into the dashboard requires Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
To integrate Pulse survey results into the Copilot Dashboard, you must have at least one of the following subscription licenses:
- Viva Suite
- Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback
- Viva Glint
- Microsoft Copilot

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price or meter for targeted audience surveys is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse targeted audience surveys pricing meter licensing. Opened measure-copilot-impact-in-your-organization, granular-access-controls and licensing-requirements; none specifies a separate targeted-surveys price or meter.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center policy-creation path is Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy.
claims.quote:
1. From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu.
2. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access.
3. Select Create a policy.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaPulse -FeatureId <FeatureId> -Name <PolicyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-default disabling policy for the selected Pulse feature.
claims.quote:
Pulse | VivaPulse
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false
If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature -ModuleId VivaPulse discovers supported Pulse features and their identifiers.
claims.quote:
Pulse | VivaPulse
Use the Get-VivaModuleFeature PowerShell cmdlet to get a list of all of the features available in a specific Microsoft 365 app and their associated IDs.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The in-app recipient-threshold path is Manage > Privacy > Minimum number of recipients and responses > Minimum recipients.
claims.quote:
In the Manage tab, go to the Privacy tab.
Under the Minimum number of recipients and responses heading go to the Minimum recipients section, where you can select a value between 3 and 25 using either the caret or typing in the value.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for setting the Viva Pulse minimum recipient count as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse minimum recipients privacy setting API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; "Viva Pulse" "minimum recipients" "API" "PowerShell". Read in-app setup, granular access controls and Viva policy documentation; no threshold-setting API found.

claims.claim: The Viva Pulse admin role manages the in-app minimum recipient setting.
claims.quote: The Viva Pulse in-app experience can be managed by users with the Viva Pulse admin role.

claims.claim: The minimum recipient setting accepts values from 3 to 25.
claims.quote: The minimum value allowed is 3 and maximum value allowed is 25.

claims.claim: Feature access management can control targeted audience surveys at tenant scope.
claims.quote: For all of the features below, admins can use centralized feature access management to determine access at the tenant level

claims.claim: The minimum recipient threshold is an organisation-wide setting.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can set privacy options for your organization. This includes setting the minimum number of recipients required to send a pulse

claims.claim: Viva Insights builds the audience from filters applied on the Readiness, Adoption or Impact tab.
claims.quote: Select the Readiness, Adoption, or Impact tab, and apply any filters you want the survey audience selection to follow.

claims.claim: The dashboard survey button shows the filtered audience size.
claims.quote: If you've applied dashboard filters (example: organization or job function), the audience is narrowed to the people who match those filters, and the button shows how many users match.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Individual pre-built group member identities are never shown to the author or in the report.
claims.quote: The pre-built audience groups are privacy-protected groups: Individual member identities are never revealed to the author or in the report.

claims.claim: Record named responses is off and cannot be enabled for pre-built audience groups.
claims.quote: Record named responses is turned off and can't be enabled — responses from a pre-built audience group are always confidential.

claims.claim: Only one pre-built audience group can be used per survey.
claims.quote: Only one pre-built audience group can be used per survey.

claims.claim: A survey is not offered to audiences below the organisation's Pulse minimum recipient count.
claims.quote: The audience must meet your organization's minimum recipient count, which your Viva Pulse admin sets under Admin settings > Confidentiality. The survey isn't offered to audiences below the minimum.

claims.claim: Learn marks pre-built audience groups as Public Preview.
claims.quote: Pre-built audience groups are available in Public Preview.

claims.claim: MC1446805 was updated on 28 October 2026.
claims.quote: Updated October 28, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required to enable the feature.
claims.quote: No action is required to enable this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Learn requires leader access directly or as a delegate; other managers can add recipients manually but cannot use pre-built groups.
claims.quote: You have leader access to the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, either directly or as a delegate. Other Managers can send a Pulse by manually adding audience but cannot use the pre-built groups.

claims.quote:
Select the survey button, for example Start Copilot Impact survey for active users.
Viva Pulse opens with the Copilot template and the audience already added.
Finish and send the Pulse.

claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse targeted audience surveys frequency limit same recipients leader; "Viva Pulse" "limit" "send" "frequency". Read feature limitations, granular controls and in-app setup; no applicable survey-frequency cap found.

claims.claim: Leaders can still send Copilot surveys to manually chosen recipients when the targeted-audience feature is off.

claims.quote: Existing surveys that were already sent to a pre-built audience are unaffected, and their reports remain available.

claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review who holds the CxO or CxO-delegate role ... and remove anyone who should not survey the whole Copilot population.' Table rows cover only pre-built audience availability and minimum recipient count.
claims.fix: Append to the role-review checklist item: 'Role-assignment management is not covered by the controls table.' Do not add a control row.
